arxiv-2106-13919.title: Pruning Edges and Gradients to Learn Hypergraphs from Larger Sets
arxiv-2106-13919.creator: David W. Zhang, Gertjan J. Burghouts, Cees G. M. Snoek
arxiv-2106-13919.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by David W. Zhang, Gertjan J. Burghouts, Cees G. M. Snoek. This paper aims for set-to-hypergraph prediction, where the goal is to infer the set of relations for a given set of entities. This is a common abstraction for applications in particle physics, biological systems, and combinatorial optimization. We address two common scaling problems encountered in set-to-hypergraph tasks that limit the size of the input set: the exponentially growing number of hyperedges and the run-time complexity, both leading to higher memory requirements.

arxiv-2109-03966.title: Sensitive Samples Revisited: Detecting Neural Network Attacks Using Constraint Solvers Thanks: Partially supported by the US National Science Foundation under grant # SaTC-1929300. Affiliation: Khoury College of Computer Sciences, Northeastern University, Boston, USA
arxiv-2109-03966.creator: Amel Nestor Docena Thomas Wahl Trevor Pearce Yunsi Fei
arxiv-2109-03966.description: Abstract Neural Networks are used today in numerous security- and safety-relevant domains and are, as such, a popular target of attacks that subvert their classification capabilities, by manipulating the network parameters. Prior work has introduced sensitive samples —inputs highly sensitive to parameter changes—to detect such manipulations, and proposed a gradient ascent-based approach to compute them.

arxiv-2111-14455.title: Information diagrams in the study of entanglement in symmetric multi-quDit systems and applications to quantum phase transitions in Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick D-level atom models
arxiv-2111-14455.creator: Julio Guerrero, Alberto Mayorgas, Manuel Calixto
arxiv-2111-14455.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Julio Guerrero, Alberto Mayorgas, Manuel Calixto. In this paper we pursue the use of information measures (in particular, information diagrams) for the study of entanglement in symmetric multi-quDit systems. We use generalizations to U ⁡ ( D ) \mathrm{U}(D) of spin U ⁡ ( 2 ) \mathrm{U}(2) coherent states and their adaptation to parity (multicomponent Schrödinger cats) and we analyse one- and two-quDit reduced density matrices.

arxiv-2202-10881.title: Coordinate-Aligned Multi-Camera Collaboration for Active Multi-Object Tracking
arxiv-2202-10881.creator: Zeyu Fang ∗, Jian Zhao ∗, Mingyu Yang, Wengang Zhou, Zhenbo Lu, Houqiang Li
arxiv-2202-10881.description: Abstract Active Multi-Object Tracking (AMOT) is a task where cameras are controlled by a centralized system to adjust their poses automatically and collaboratively so as to maximize the coverage of targets in their shared visual field. In AMOT, each camera only receives partial information from its observation, which may mislead cameras to take locally optimal action.

arxiv-2206-01308.title: A new Microscopic Model for J / ψ J/\psi Production in Heavy Ion Collisions
arxiv-2206-01308.creator: Denys Yen Arrebato Villar, Jiaxing Zhao, Joerg Aichelin, Pol Bernard Gossiaux
arxiv-2206-01308.description: Abstract We present a new model for the creation of J / ψ J/\psi mesons in ultrarelativistic heavy ion collisions, which allows to follow the individual heavy quarks from their creation until the detector through the Quark Gluon Plasma (QGP), which is formed in these collisions and described by the EPOS2 event generator.

arxiv-2210-02072.title: Optimal Control of the F 1 -ATPase Molecular Motor
arxiv-2210-02072.creator: Deepak Gupta, Steven J. Large, Shoichi Toyabe, David A. Sivak
arxiv-2210-02072.description: Abstract F 1 -ATPase is a rotary molecular motor that in vivo is subject to strong nonequilibrium driving forces. There is great interest in understanding the operational principles governing its high efficiency of free-energy transduction. Here we use a near-equilibrium framework to design a non-trivial control protocol to minimize dissipation in rotating F 1 \mathrm{F}_{1} to synthesize ATP.

arxiv-2210-11902.title: Non-parametric adaptive bandwidth selection for kernel estimators
arxiv-2210-11902.creator: of spatial intensity functions
arxiv-2210-11902.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by of spatial intensity functions. Abstract: We propose a new fully non-parametric two-step adaptive bandwidth selection method for kernel estimators of spatial point process intensity functions based on the Campbell–Mecke formula and Abramson’s square root law. We present a simulation study to assess its performance relative to the Cronie–Van Lieshout global bandwidth selector and apply the technique to data on induced earthquakes in the Groningen gas field. AMS Mathematics Subject Classification (2010): 60G55; 60D05; 62M30.

arxiv-2212-10253.title: Material surfaces in stochastic flows: integrals of motion and intermittency
arxiv-2212-10253.creator: A.S. Il’yn 1,2 , A.V. Kopyev ∗ , V.A. Sirota, K.P. Zybin 1,2
arxiv-2212-10253.description: Abstract We consider the line, surface and volume elements of fluid in stationary isotropic incompressible stochastic flow in d d -dimensional space and investigate the long-time evolution of their statistic properties. We report the discovery of a family of d ! − 1 d!

arxiv-2310-18957.title: Weighted frames, weighted lower semi frames and unconditionally convergent multipliers
arxiv-2310-18957.creator: P. Balazs, R. Corso, D. Stoeva
arxiv-2310-18957.description: Abstract In this paper we ask when it is possible to transform a given sequence into a frame or a lower semi frame by multiplying the elements by numbers. In other words, we ask when a given sequence is a weighted frame or a weighted lower semi frame and for each case we formulate a conjecture.

arxiv-2311-13698.title: A blueprint for truncation resonance placement in elastic periodic lattices with unit cell asymmetry
arxiv-2311-13698.creator: Hasan B. Al Ba’ba’a, Hosam Yousef, Mostafa Nouh
arxiv-2311-13698.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hasan B. Al Ba’ba’a, Hosam Yousef, Mostafa Nouh. Elastic periodic lattices act as mechanical filters of incident vibrational loads. By and large, they forbid wave propagation within bandgaps and resonate outside them. However, they often encounter ‘truncation resonances’ inside bandgaps when certain conditions are met.

arxiv-2403-19005.title: The bending rigidity exponent of a two-dimensional crystalline membrane with arbitrary number of flexural phonon modes
arxiv-2403-19005.creator: D. A. Ivanov, A. Kudlis, I. S. Burmistrov
arxiv-2403-19005.description: Abstract We investigate the elastic behavior of two-dimensional crystalline membrane embedded into real space taking into account the presence an arbitrary number of flexural phonon modes d c d_{c} (the number of out-of-plane deformation field components). The bending rigidity exponent η \eta is extracted by numerical simulation via Fourier Monte Carlo technique of the system behaviour in the universal regime.

arxiv-2503-22288.title: SimDC: A High-Fidelity Device Simulation Platform for Device-Cloud Collaborative Computing
arxiv-2503-22288.creator: Ruiguang Pei 1, Junjie Wu 1, Dan Peng, Min Fang, Jianan Zhang, Zhihui Fu 2, Jun Wang 2
arxiv-2503-22288.description: Abstract The advent of edge intelligence and escalating concerns for data privacy protection have sparked a surge of interest in device-cloud collaborative computing. Large-scale device deployments to validate prototype solutions are often prohibitively expensive and practically challenging, resulting in a pronounced demand for simulation tools that can emulate real-world scenarios.

arxiv-2505-08585.title: A Large-scale Benchmark on Geological Fault Delineation Models: Domain Shift, Training Dynamics, Generalizability, Evaluation and Inferential Behavior
arxiv-2505-08585.creator: JORGE QUESADA 1, CHEN ZHOU 1, PRITHWIJIT CHOWDHURY 1, MOHAMMAD ALOTAIBI 1, AHMAD MUSTAFA 2, YUSUFJON KUMAKOV 3, MOHIT PRABHUSHANKAR (MEMBER, IEEE) 1, GHASSAN ALREGIB (FELLOW, IEEE) 1
arxiv-2505-08585.description: Abstract Machine learning has taken a critical role in seismic interpretation workflows, especially in fault delineation tasks. However, despite the recent proliferation of pretrained models and synthetic datasets, the field still lacks a systematic understanding of the generalizability limits of these models across seismic data representing a variety of geologic, acquisition and processing settings.

arxiv-2511-18918.title: Optimization-Aware Test Generation for Deep Learning Compilers Conference: 2026 IEEE/ACM 48th International Conference on Software Engineering; April 12–18, 2026; Rio de Janeiro, Brazil 2026 IEEE/ACM 48th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE ’26), April 12–18, 2026, Rio de Janeiro,
arxiv-2511-18918.creator: Qingchao Shen 1 , Zan Wang 1 , Haoyang Ma 2 , Yongqiang Tian 3 , Lili Huang 1 , Zibo Xiao 1 Junjie Chen 1,* , Shing-Chi Cheung 2
arxiv-2511-18918.description: Abstract . Deep Learning (DL) compilers have been widely utilized to optimize DL models for efficient deployment across various hardware. Due to their vital role in the DL ecosystem, ensuring their reliability is critical. Such model optimizations are often designed to match specific computational graph structures.

arxiv-2511-21907.title: Homogenization and linearization in magnetoelasticity under small elastic response
arxiv-2511-21907.creator: Mikhail Cherdantsev, Elisa Davoli, Lorenza D’Elia, Samuele Riccò
arxiv-2511-21907.description: Abstract . We perform a simultaneous homogenization and linearization analysis for a magnetoelastic energy functional featuring a mixed Eulerian-Lagrangian structure. Neglecting Zeeman and anisotropic contributions, we characterize the asymptotic behavior in the sense of Gamma-convergence for the sum of a nonlinear magnetoelastic energy, a symmetric exchange term defined on the actual configuration, and for the associated magnetostatic self-energy.

europmc-pmc4167952.title: Peripheral nerve reconstruction after injury: a review of clinical and experimental therapies.
europmc-pmc4167952.creator: Grinsell D, Keating CP.
europmc-pmc4167952.description: Unlike other tissues in the body, peripheral nerve regeneration is slow and usually incomplete. Less than half of patients who undergo nerve repair after injury regain good to excellent motor or sensory function and current surgical techniques are similar to those described by...

plos-pone-0008901.creator: Christophe Boesch, Camille Bolé, Nadin Eckhardt et al.
plos-pone-0008901.description: PLOS ONE research article. In recent years, extended altruism towards unrelated group members has been proposed to be a unique characteristic of human societies. Support for this proposal seemingly came from experimental studies on captive chimpanzees that showed that individuals were limited in the ways t

pmc-11435113.title: Is Obesity a Problem in New Cystic Fibrosis Treatments?
pmc-11435113.creator: Marta Solís-García, Marta María García-Clemente, Claudia Janeth Madrid-Carbajal, Adrián Peláez, Rosa Mar Gómez Punter, Jose María Eiros Bachiller, Rosa María Girón Moreno
pmc-11435113.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction: Malnutrition has always been a problem in CF (cystic fibrosis) patients; however, new treatments with CFTR (cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator protein) modulators have led to weight gain, with some patients at risk of overweight and obesity. Objective: Our study aimed to analyze the evolution of BMI (body mass index) after one year of treatment with triple therapy and the factors associated with weight gain in CF patients undergoing treatment with triple therapy with CFTR protein modulators (ETI) (elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor).

pmc-11674048.title: First-Line (1L) Treatment Decision Patterns and Survival of Hormone Receptor (HR)-Positive/HER2-Negative Advanced Breast Cancer (ABC) Patients in a Latin American (LATAM) Public Institution
pmc-11674048.creator: Guillermo Valencia, Patricia Rioja, Miguel Chirito, Olenka Peralta, Jorge Sánchez, Connie Rabanal, Raúl Mantilla, Zaida Morante, Hugo Fuentes, Carlos Castaneda, Tatiana Vidaurre, Cristian Pacheco, Silvia Neciosup, Henry L Gomez
pmc-11674048.description: Advanced breast cancer is an incurable disease, with a median overall survival of 3 years, including in countries without access problems. Although chemotherapy is reserved in some cases, it is still used in many countries as a first-line therapy. The aim of our study is to evaluate the first-line treatment choices and the factors that influence therapeutic decisions.

pmc-11717538.title: Stories of taking part in Everyday Life Rehabilitation - A narrative inquiry of residents with serious mental illness and their recovery pathway
pmc-11717538.creator: Rosaline Bezerra Aguiar, Maria Lindström
pmc-11717538.description: Context and purposePersons enduring serious mental illness (SMI) and living in supported housing facilities often receive inadequate care, which can negatively impact their health outcomes. To address these challenges, it is crucial to prioritize interventions that promote personal recovery and address the unique needs of this group.

pmc-12638735.title: From Risk and Vulnerability to Preparedness and Resiliency: An Opinion Piece on Championing Disaster and Emergency Risk Reduction and Management in Kidney Care
pmc-12638735.creator: Shaifali Sandal, Saly El Wazze, Caroline E Stigant, Terri Chanda, WA David Berry, Isabelle Ethier, Kristen Pederson, Neil Finkle, Ratna Samanta, Michael Gagnon, Tamara Glavinovic, Drew Hager, Jay Hingwala, Matthew Hunt, Seychelle Yohanna, Jennifer M McRae, Naomi Martens, Laura Horowitz, Catherine We
pmc-12638735.description: 25 Introduction A disaster is a “serious disruption of the functioning of a community or a society at any scale due to hazardous events interacting with conditions of exposure, vulnerability, and capacity, leading to one or more of the following: human, material, economic, and environmental losses and impacts.

pmc-12639343.title: Clinician Perspectives on Incorporating Physical Activity and Sleep Prescriptions Using eHealth for Youth With Comorbid Psychiatric Disorders: Qualitative Focus Group Study
pmc-12639343.creator: Alyssa M Button, James Slavet, Amanda E Staiano, April B Bowling
pmc-12639343.description: BackgroundPhysical activity and sleep prescriptions are indicated for the treatment of psychiatric disorders among youth. However, there is limited clinical adoption of these practices. Exergaming (ie, games that require physical activity) is a feasible intervention to promote physical activity and sleep hygiene and is appealing to youth given their interest in video gaming.

pmc-13000722.title: An alkaline nanosized platelet vesicle-based hydrogel for the treatment of osteoporotic bone defects
pmc-13000722.creator: Ke Yang, Yang Yang, Chen Xia, Yiyu Chen, Zhanqiu Dai, Zijie Wang, Lintao Hu, Yijun Li, Yongcheng Wang, Yining Wang, Wenshuai Li, Qingqing Wang, Na Li, Shuqi Jiang, Shouyan Zu, Feng Hao, Qichen Shen, Shunwu Fan, Pengfei Chen, Liqing Shangguan, Lei Ning
pmc-13000722.description: Osteoporosis is a systemic bone disease in which excessive differentiation of osteoclasts leads to reduced bone mass, weakened bone microstructure, and increased fragility. These overactive osteoclasts require low lysosomal pH to function. Therefore, alkalinizing lysosome represents a potential therapeutic strategy for osteoporotic bone defects. Recently, platelet-derived nanovesicles have shown promise in tissue repair and drug delivery.

pmc-13035700.title: Machine learning in cancer imaging for enhanced precision in diagnosis and therapy
pmc-13035700.creator: James C. L. Chow
pmc-13035700.description: Machine learning (ML) is transforming cancer imaging by enhancing diagnosis, automating image analysis, and improving treatment planning. This review explores key ML applications, including tumor detection, radiomics, multi-modal imaging, and therapy monitoring. We discuss fundamental ML techniques, deep learning architectures, and data preprocessing strategies essential for medical imaging.

pmc-13094073.title: Short-term outcomes of health belief model-based brief virtual education on HPV infection and vaccination among pharmacy students: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13094073.creator: Sümeyye Kavak, Abdikarim Abdi, Pınar Ay, Yeliz Şahin, Mesut Sancar, Betul Okuyan
pmc-13094073.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundGenital Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection was a global public health concern, with low vaccination rates in Türkiye highlighting a critical need for effective interventions. Pharmacists, as future health advocates, were a crucial target population. This study evaluated the short-term outcomes of brief virtual education program based on the Health Belief Model (HBM) on pharmacy students’ knowledge and health beliefs on HPV infection and vaccination.MethodsA randomized controlled trial with a pre-test/post-test design was conducted with pharmacy students in Istanbul, Türkiye.

pmc-13139417.title: A retrospective clinical risk prediction model for co‑infection with Mycoplasma pneumoniae in patients with COVID‑19 based on restricted cubic splines
pmc-13139417.creator: Kailong Ye, Yanling Su, Xiaoqing Hu, Xiu Chen, Bin Song, Qinghua Zhang, Hui Lin, Linmiao Zeng, Yiqun Dai, Jianhong Xiao
pmc-13139417.description: Co-infection with Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) represents a clinically significant complication that often leads to prolonged hospital stay, increased mortality risk, and a higher demand for mechanical ventilation. This study constructed a risk prediction model for early identification of SARS-CoV-2 and MP co-infections. We retrospectively analyzed SARS-CoV-2 patients admitted between December 2022 and February 2023.

pmc-13356849.title: Nanofiber Matrix Dressing for Split-Thickness Skin Graft Donor Sites: A Randomized Comparative Clinical Study
pmc-13356849.creator: Maciej Biskupski, Sergey Antonov, Zofia Małgorzata Górecka, Rafał Wójcik, Katarzyna Żuchowska, Marek Majewski, Kamil Torres
pmc-13356849.description: BackgroundDonor-site morbidity after split-thickness skin graft (STSG) harvest remains a significant clinical concern, with pain representing one of the most burdensome early postoperative symptoms. Electrospun nanofiber matrices have emerged as a promising wound management strategy, yet clinical evidence supporting their use in STSG donor sites remains limited.

pmc-13372762.title: The determination of human creative thinking by employing machine learning classification on EEG signals
pmc-13372762.creator: Jilin Zou, Fang Yuan, Silin Zhou, Jiaqin Yang, Chunlei Liu
pmc-13372762.description: Background and objectiveTraditional creativity assessments are limited by subjectivity and high labor costs. Although machine learning (ML) offers objective alternatives, its application to EEG-based creativity evaluation remains scarce. This study aimed to classify high and low creative thinking from EEG signals using ML.MethodsOne hundred forty participants completed the Alternative Uses Task during EEG recording.

pmc-13610105.title: Clinical Translation of Fisetin for Age-Related Diseases: Current Evidence and Future Opportunities
pmc-13610105.creator: Carolina Sandoval-Caballero, Zander Roemer, Catherine M. Kotz, Michael A. Puskarich, Vijayakumar Mavanji, Elizabeth L. Schmidt, Shalamar D. Sibley
pmc-13610105.description: Fisetin, a naturally occurring flavonoid, has garnered interest as a potential intervention for age-related diseases due to its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and senolytic properties, as demonstrated primarily in preclinical studies. We conducted a structured search and evaluated human translational and clinical studies that utilize fisetin to improve clinical markers associated with age-related low-grade inflammatory diseases.
